turns.content: Living matter contains 15.3 micrograms of total carbon, while a fossilized wood sample contains 2.4 micrograms of total carbon. Treat their ratio as the fraction of carbon-14 remaining in the wood.
Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5760 years. Write the exponential decay law, convert the half-life to seconds using 365 days per year, and calculate the decay constant in s^-1.
Use the remaining fraction and the linear-depletion law to solve algebraically for the elapsed time since the wood stopped exchanging carbon with its surroundings.
Evaluate the calendar-calibrated age in seconds and convert it to an approximate age in years.
Independently express the observed activity ratio as a number of elapsed half-lives and use that route to check the age obtained above.
State the checked age and explain, for positive radioactive decay, how a lower remaining activity changes the inferred elapsed time.
Substitute the checked age back into A=A_0 exp(-kt) to verify the observed activity ratio, and confirm the qualitative activity-age direction.
Report the final age in seconds and years, together with the activity-age interpretation.
